title: SLO Cadence Bootcamp & Cross-functional Rehearsal Notebook
body:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for a compact, operational-first SLO cadence bootcamp aimed at product, infra, platform, and support partners. The goal is not to write another policy doc — its to rehearse precise handoffs, validate signals, and train responders on the SLO rhythm we expect teams to run for model-serving features (hosted API, dedicated, private).

Objective (measurable):
- Run a 10-person cross-team rehearsal and complete 3 tabletop-to-live escalation handoffs within 2 weeks.
- Validate the SLO signal chain end-to-end (client metric -> aggregators -> alert -> incident bridge -> postmortem starter).
- Produce 5 small, actionable changes to the SLO observability checklist and 2 quick configuration changes (alert thresholds, runbook links).

Audience:
- SREs, Feature Engineers owning model endpoints, Platform Engineers, Customer Success on-call leads, Product PMs for priority features.

High-level bootcamp plan (2 weeks):
Week 0 (prep)
- Day -7: Invite list, pre-reading, attach current SLOs + incident runbooks, mapping doc.
- Day -5: Data sanity check run: make sure metrics exporter, rollups, and alerting queries are returning expected values.
- Day -3: Quick sync with observability infra to enable synthetic tests and a short-lived alert channel for the rehearsal.

Week 1 (rehearsals)
- Day 1: Orientation (1 hour): cadence overview, roles, how to read SLO dashboards.
- Day 2-3: Tabletop sessions (2x 90m) focused on: slow tail latency (P95->P99 divergence) and token-cost regression. Use incident-sculpting templates (see exercises section).
- Day 4: Live mini-sim (4 hours): inject synthetic latency to a staging model pool and exercise automated fallback routing. Observe system kinetics, KV cache warm-up effects, request batching shifts.
- Day 5: Debrief and quick fixes (2 hours): triage suggested changes and apply 2 configuration items in staging.

Week 2 (handoff & measurement)
- Day 8: Canary failure escalation (full replay): simulate a sustained GPU pool failure in a single region and route traffic to fallback variant. Walk the oncall rota through the escalation.
- Day 10: Customer-impact tabletop (90m): product PM and CS run prioritization decisions (who to call, customer comms).
- Day 12: Postmortem starter & metrics audit (2 hours): ensure the postmortem stub has required SLO evidence and signal artifacts.

Session roles and responsibilities (short form):
- Incident Commander (IC): SRE oncall (primary). Starts bridge, drives tl;dr, ensures runbook steps executed.
- Observability Lead: platform-observability engineer. Owns dashboards, ensures alerts fired and screenshots are captured.
- Feature Owner: product/feature engineer for the affected endpoint. Executes rollback/fallback if required, decision authority for product trade-offs.
- Routing/Fallback Engineer: serving-runtime engineer. Validates model variant/fallback routing and capacity changes.
- CS Rep: customer-success oncall lead. Prepares communication template and customer impact assessment.
- Recorder/PM: takes notes, timestamps key signal artifacts for postmortem.

Exercises (unique, repeatable):
1) Incident Sculpting: P95->P99 Divergence
- Scenario: After a model update, P95 stays stable but P99 latency spikes for long-tail queries. No immediate request drop, but error budgets are bleeding.
- Steps:
  - Observability Lead runs the "tail-sampler" query (provided snippet) to collect full-request histograms.
  - IC declares SLO burn threshold; Feature Owner decides between throttling long queries or rolling back.
  - Routing Engineer toggles prefix-KV caching to test mitigation; measure 15-minute impact.
- Learning targets: how quickly can teams identify root-cause (model complexity vs batching behavior), and can fallback routing prevent escalation within 20 minutes.

2) Model Serving Cost Spike (token-cost regression)
- Scenario: A change increases token churn for a set of prompts causing 2x cost on a mid-tier route and a steady SLO burn on latency under load.
- Steps:
  - Use recorded traffic replay in a staging pool for 30 minutes.
  - Observability Lead shows token-cost attribution per route; CS flags customers at risk.
  - Quick mitigations: reduce max_tokens, enable quantized variant for that route, or apply rate limiting.
- Learning targets: map cost signal to SLO choices and runbook entries.

3) Partial-region GPU Failure + Fallback Validation
- Scenario: One region's dedicated pool loses 60% capacity over 10 minutes (simulated), autoscaler triggers but not fast enough.
- Steps:
  - Routing/Fallback Engineer force-routes 20% traffic to secondary region/model variant.
  - IC checks latency and errors on radar; if customer-impacting, CS drafts comms.
- Learning targets: time-to-fallback, warm-up cost, and customer impact communication template timing.

Rehearsal scripts (short snippets you can read out):
- "Bridge open. We see P99 at 2.4s for route X, error rate stable. Token cost has increased 2.1x for the last 10m. IC asks: Feature owner, do you own rollback or do we throttle?"
- "Observability: attaching dashboard snapshot and flame graph link. Routing, can you confirm fallback candidate is ready?"

Artifacts to capture during runs (must be saved to the incident folder):
- Dashboard screenshots with timestamped queries.
- Alert firing history (raw JSON).
- Sampling of raw traces and the input prompts that caused the tail.
- Command history for any toggles (rolling back, routing changes).

Success metrics and acceptance criteria:
- All alert-to-bridge times <= 5 minutes for synthetic tests.
- At least 1 successful automated fallback during live mini-sim with < 15% customer-impact traffic diverted.
- Post-bootcamp: 80% of participants can list the SLO signal chain in a 3-point checklist test.

Quick runbook checklist (bite-sized items):
- Is the correct SLO policy attached to the route? (yes/no)
- Can synthetic tests be triggered in < 10m? (who owns it)
- Alert severity mapping set: P99 latency -> page; error-rate -> page; cost-spike -> slack only.
- Postmortem stub created with links to dashboards, alert JSONs, and timeline.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- TODO: Get explicit buy-in from Product for automated rollback on canary model updates (Marco).
- TODO: Validate synthetic load harness for token-cost tests (Lina).
- Question: should cost-spike alerts page SRE or only alert CS+product first? (discuss in debrief).
- TODO: Add a short "customer-impact rubric" to runbooks so CS can rapidly classify impacted tenants.

Debrief template (use after every rehearsal):
- What worked? (top 3)
- What blocked the run? (top 3)
- Quick fixes applied during the run (list + owner)
- Follow-ups and owners (JIRA tickets recommended)

Appendix: handy queries & snippets (copy-paste friendly)
- Tail-sampler (pseudo):
  SELECT bucket, count FROM request_latency_histogram WHERE route = 'api/model-x' SINCE -15m
- Token-cost attribution (pseudo):
  SELECT sum(tokens*cost_per_token) BY route WHERE time > -1h
- Bridge start template (slack):
  "Bridge open: slo-bootcamp: route X, P99 2.4s, error-rate 0.12%. IC: @oncall-sre. Observability: @obs-lead. Feature: @feature-owner. Recording on."

Appendix B: short rehearsal checklist for participants (one-pager to print):
- Bring laptop, ensure VPN access to staging project.
- Confirm you have access to incident folder and alert logs.
- Read the SLO one-pager (2 minutes).
- Be ready to be assigned IC or Observability roles during a run.

Revision history (quick):
- 2026-01-15 created initial bootcamp notebook (Aisha).
- 2026-01-22 added fallback validation exercise and success metrics (Marco).
- 2026-02-10 updated linked artifact references and added debrief template (Aisha).

Notes (informal):
- This is intentionally lean: emphasize runs over long design debates. Keep scripts short and actionable.
- If product is uncomfortable with automated rollback, focus on fast throttles and explicit customer comm windows.
- Keep the incident folder tidy: attach a single JSON timeline and up to 5 representative traces.

End of notebook.
